title: Which of 23, 51, 37 and 26 are prime numbers?
description: Four numbers are tested by looking for a factor pair other than one and the number itself. Two of them split into smaller numbers and two do not.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is composite as soon as one factor pair other than one and itself is found, and it is prime when none exists. Watch for students who call fifty one prime because it is odd.

video_script.why: The child sorts four numbers into prime and composite by looking for a factor pair, the way the numbers from twenty one to thirty were sorted in the book.
video_script.substitution: Look for a factor pair other than one and the number for each of the four numbers.
video_script.anchor: Four number cards on the board, each waiting to be sorted into prime or composite
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty three and thirty seven are prime, and fifty one and twenty six are composite.

final_answer.spoken: only twenty three and thirty seven are prime

maths_rules: 23: 2, 3, 4, 5 do not divide it exactly (23 = 2 × 11 + 1, 23 = 3 × 7 + 2, 23 = 4 × 5 + 3, 23 = 5 × 4 + 3), so 23 has only the factors 1 and 23 and is prime
37: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 do not divide it exactly (37 = 2 × 18 + 1, 3 × 12 + 1, 4 × 9 + 1, 5 × 7 + 2, 6 × 6 + 1), so 37 has only the factors 1 and 37 and is prime
video_script.design: Each number card gets a factor pair beside it, or a row of failed tries, and then turns amber or teal.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about prime numbers.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Four numbers are given, twenty three, fifty one, thirty seven and twenty six.

beats.on_screen: the four number cards stay on the board

beats.on_screen: Prime = exactly two factors, 1 and itself. One factor pair other than 1 and itself makes a number composite.

marks.pair: a factor pair other than one and itself lights up
marks.same: the numbers from twenty one to thirty appear as an example

narration: <bookmark mark='prime'/>A prime number has exactly two factors, one and the number itself.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>If we find one more factor pair, the number is composite.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We sorted the numbers from twenty one to thirty this way.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers twenty three, fifty one, thirty seven and twenty six.

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of them are prime.

marks.twenty: twenty six splits into two times thirteen and turns amber
marks.fifty: fifty one splits into three times seventeen and turns amber

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step one, look for a factor pair. Twenty six is two times thirteen, so it is composite.
<bookmark mark='fifty'/>Fifty one is three times seventeen, so fifty one is composite too, even though it is odd.

beats.on_screen: 23: tries 2, 3, 4, 5 all leave a remainder; 37: tries 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 all leave a remainder

marks.tw: the tries for twenty three are written, and each leaves a remainder
marks.th: the tries for thirty seven are written, and each leaves a remainder

narration: <bookmark mark='tw'/>Step two, try small numbers on twenty three. Two, three, four and five each leave a remainder.
<bookmark mark='th'/>Try two, three, four, five and six on thirty seven. Each of them leaves a remainder as well.

beats.on_screen: Check: 23 has only the factors 1 and 23; 37 has only the factors 1 and 37; 3 × 17 = 51 and 2 × 13 = 26

marks.two: the two factor lists are written
marks.back: the two products are multiplied back to fifty one and twenty six

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, check the result. Twenty three and thirty seven have only two factors each.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Three times seventeen is fifty one. Two times thirteen is twenty six, so those factor pairs are right.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 23 and 37 are prime; 51 and 26 are composite
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Twenty three and thirty seven are prime, and fifty one and twenty six are composite.
